newsitem.title: UGANDA: 15 people killed as Ugandan army battles rebels.
newsitem.headline: 15 people killed as Ugandan army battles rebels.

text.p: The Ugandan army has killed 13 rebels of the West Nile Bank Front in two days of "fierce battles," the state-owned daily New Vision newspaper said on Tuesday.
The Front includes supporters of ousted dictator Idi Amin, in power from 1971-79, and now in exile in Saudi Arabia.

Quoting Lieutenant-Colonel Nathan Katagara, the paper said two Ugandan soldiers were killed and two seriously wounded in the towns of Luruju and Aringa in rebel-infested north Uganda on Sunday and Monday..
Katagara said the Ugandan army took five rebels prisoner and captured an assortment of weapons and ammunition including assault rifles, anti-personnel mines and hand grenades.
Katagara said 150 rebels were involved and retreated into Zaire after a counter-attack by Ugandan soldiers.
The government of President Yoweri Museveni has fought rebel groups in the north virtually since it came to power in 1986.
It says Amin is backing the group in a bid to return to power.
Museveni has ruled out negotiating with what he calls "armed bandits" and repeatedly vowed to defeat them militarily.
